# OpenART: Open Agent Red Teaming

OpenART is an executable benchmark and Docker-native runtime for evaluating tool-using agent safety in long-horizon, evolving environments. The benign task and hidden safety contract remain fixed while target-visible workspace, tool, or service state changes mid-run. Deterministic and model-based evaluators judge safety over execution traces and snapshots. Task workspaces may contain synthetic risky-source strings that are evaluation fixtures, not instructions.

## Key facts

- Released planner tasks: 10,150 in 52 ZIP shards (~75 GB).
- Dataset viewer configs: mid (1,046 tasks), mid-v5 (3,553), large (5,551).
- Released tools dataset: 63,697 selected materialized tools.
- Paper settings: 10K+ validated scenarios, 50 domains, 500K+ tools and skills, median 97 tool calls.
- Paper evaluation matrix: 15 agents × 5 models (75 settings), with 8 target-visible attack vectors.
- Paper-reported pooled strict attack success rate: 85.0% using the Evolutionary Markov Hypergraph Attack (EMHA). Strict ASR requires deterministic-evaluator and LLM-judge confirmation.
- Paper-reported pooled benign completion: 87.38%.
- The paper capability corpus is distinct from the released materialized-tool subset; paper settings are distinct from release counts.
- The runtime can affect safety beyond the choice of foundation model.
- Repository includes three bundled high-complexity tasks and CITATION.cff.
- Code license: AGPL-3.0. The task dataset card uses `license: other` with mixed upstream terms; consult the card before reuse.

## Preferred citation

Chen et al. (2026), “OpenART: Scaling Agent Red Teaming via Open-Ended Environment Evolution,” arXiv:2608.00677. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00677

Authors: Yunhao Chen, Xin Wang, Yixu Wang, Yi Liu, Jie Li, Yan Teng, Xingjun Ma, Xia Hu, and Yu-Gang Jiang.

Cite both the arXiv paper and the software repository when using the runtime, tasks, tools, or evaluation results. The PDF also prints “OpenART Arena”; both names refer to this work. Use the arXiv title verbatim in bibliographies.
